violations.summary: An issue was discovered in pip (all versions) because it installs the version with the highest version number, even if the user had intended to obtain a private package from a private index. This only affects use of the --extra-index-url option, and exploitation requires that the package does not already exist in the public index (and thus the attacker can put the package there with an arbitrary version number). NOTE: it has been reported that this is intended functionality and the user is responsible for using --extra-index-url securely

extended_information.short_description: pip could download private packages from a public PyPI repository leading to code execution.
extended_information.full_description:
This CVE refers to the possibility of a "dependency confusion" attack when using `pip` with the `--extra-index-url` flag. This vulnerability has been disputed by the maintainers of pip as the described behavior is intended (although potentially insecure) and as such there are no plans to fix it. 

If pip is executed with the `--extra-index-url` when using a private PyPI repository, an attacker could cause pip to download a private package (for example one named `private_package`) by adding a package with the same name (`private_package`) in the public PyPI repository. This would lead to remote code execution as pip will download the public package that could contain malicious code. This dependency confusion attack was [demonstrated in 2021 by Alex Birsan](https://medium.com/@alex.birsan/dependency-confusion-4a5d60fec610).

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The issue has been disputed by the vendor
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: Pip maintainers, and others such as [RHEL](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2018-20225) do not consider this a vulnerability as it is the intended behaviour

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The issue results in a severe impact (such as remote code execution)
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: A malicious package can contain arbitrary code, which is by definition a severe code execution impact

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: Exploitation of the issue is only possible when the vulnerable component is used in a specific manner. The attacker has to perform per-target research to determine the vulnerable attack vector
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: Exploitation requires the pip client to use the `--extra-index-url` flag. The attacker must research and find the names of the "private packages" being installed by the victim, and then publish packages with the same name (but containing a malicious payload) to PyPI.

extended_information.remediation:
##### Deployment mitigations

Do not use the `--extra-index-url` flag with pip and consider using version pinning for deployments.

violations.summary:
A denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability exists in google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict() in Python, where the max_recursion_depth limit can be bypassed when parsing nested google.protobuf.Any messages.

Due to missing recursion depth accounting inside the internal Any-handling logic, an attacker can supply deeply nested Any structures that bypass the intended recursion limit, eventually exhausting Python’s recursion stack and causing a RecursionError.

The `ecdsa` PyPI package is a pure Python implementation of ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography) with support for ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm), EdDSA (Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm) and ECDH (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman). Versions 0.18.0 and prior are vulnerable to the Minerva attack. As of time of publication, no known patched version exists.
pyjwt v2.10.1 was discovered to contain weak encryption.

extended_information.short_description: Lack of minimal key length in PyJWT may lead to authorization bypass
extended_information.full_description:
It was discovered that PyJWT does not enforce any minimal key length when encoding JWT tokens.
For example, a user may encode and decode a JWT token successfully, even with an empty key -
```python
key = ''
e = jwt.encode({"foo":"bar"}, key, algorithm='HS256')
print(e)
>eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJmb28iOiJiYXIifQ._NaFhGu8tCCgBKksGBA6ADwRdKx3e9GES_KyF4A5phE

jwt.decode(e, key, algorithms=['HS256'])
> {'foo': 'bar'}
```

Using a key with a short length may lead to attackers successfully brute-forcing it, leading to them being able to modify the contents of JWT tokens that use that key, possibly leading to privilege escalation and authorization bypass.

The vulnerability was disputed (and never fixed) since the maintainers claim that the key is chosen by the application that uses the library, and is responsible for choosing a sufficiently long key.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The issue is trivial to exploit and does not require a published writeup or PoC
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: Attackers simply need to brute-force the key on an acquired JWT token, hoping that the token was created with a short (or empty) key.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: Exploitation of the issue is only possible when the vulnerable component is used in a specific manner. The attacker has to perform per-target research to determine the vulnerable attack vector
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: The vulnerability is exploitable when PyJWT is used to create JWT tokens with short keys.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The impact of exploiting the issue depends on the context of surrounding software. A severe impact such as RCE is not guaranteed.
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: The privileges acquired by brute-forcing a JWT token's key depend on how the relevant application uses that token.

violations.summary: LangChain versions up to and including 0.3.1 contain a regular expression denial-of-service (ReDoS) vulnerability in the MRKLOutputParser.parse() method (libs/langchain/langchain/agents/mrkl/output_parser.py). The parser applies a backtracking-prone regular expression when extracting tool actions from model output. An attacker who can supply or influence the parsed text (for example via prompt injection in downstream applications that pass LLM output directly into MRKLOutputParser.parse()) can trigger excessive CPU consumption by providing a crafted payload, causing significant parsing delays and a denial-of-service condition.

extended_information.short_description: A ReDoS in LangChain may lead to denial of service when processing LLM output
extended_information.full_description:
[LangChain](https://www.langchain.com/) is a framework for building agents and LLM-powered applications.
One of the capabilities that LangChain originally offered was a framework for building AI [agents](https://v03.api.js.langchain.com/modules/langchain.agents.html), which has now been largely deprecated in favor of the LangGraph implementation of agents.

One of these agents is the [ZeroShotAgent](https://v03.api.js.langchain.com/classes/langchain.agents.ZeroShotAgent.html), which was a tool-calling agent designed to be part of a MRKL chain. Because this agent uses tools, a regex was included to make sure the LLM output could be properly parsed into an action:

```
regex = (
    r"Action\s*\d*\s*:[\s]*(.*?)[\s]*Action\s*\d*\s*Input\s*\d*\s*:[\s]*(.*)"
)
```

This regex was vulnerable to a ReDoS, which means an attacker able to interact with the agent could use techniques such as prompt injection to curate the LLM output of a previous step, and then in the next iteration the regex will trigger and waste resources.

It's important to note that this was not patched, unlike the statement by official advisories. The vulnerable regex is still in use, however the entire class has been officially deprecated.

The vulnerability can be triggered when using the vulnerable `MRKLOutputParser` directly with user-supplied or user-influenced input -
```js
from langchain.agents.mrkl.output_parser import MRKLOutputParser
mrkl_output_parser = MRKLOutputParser()
mrkl_output_parser.parse(user_input)
```

Also, the vulnerability can be triggered when using the `ZeroShotAgent` with a user-supplied prompt -
```js
const agent = new ZeroShotAgent({
  llmChain: new LLMChain({
    llm: new ChatOpenAI({ model: "gpt-4o-mini", temperature: 0 }),
    prompt: ZeroShotAgent.createPrompt([new SerpAPI(), new Calculator()], {
      prefix: `foo`,
      suffix: `bar`,
      inputVariables: ["input", "agent_scratchpad"],
    }),
  }),
  allowedTools: ["search", "calculator"],
});

const result = await agent.inv...

violations.summary: Anthropic's MCP TypeScript SDK versions up to and including 1.25.1 contain a regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) vulnerability in the UriTemplate class when processing RFC 6570 exploded array patterns. The dynamically generated regular expression used during URI matching contains nested quantifiers that can trigger catastrophic backtracking on specially crafted inputs, resulting in excessive CPU consumption. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a malicious URI that causes the Node.js process to become unresponsive, leading to a denial of service.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: To exploit the vulnerability, a potential attacker must send a maliciously crafted URI with an exploded pattern to the server and have it processed by the vulnerable function or parse it into a ResourceTemplate.

violations.summary: MCP TypeScript SDK is the official TypeScript SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. Prior to 1.24.0, The Model Context Protocol (MCP) TypeScript SDK does not enable DNS rebinding protection by default for HTTP-based servers. When an HTTP-based MCP server is run on localhost without authentication with StreamableHTTPServerTransport or SSEServerTransport and has not enabled enableDnsRebindingProtection, a malicious website could exploit DNS rebinding to bypass same-origin policy restrictions and send requests to the local MCP server. This could allow an attacker to invoke tools or access resources exposed by the MCP server on behalf of the user in those limited circumstances. Note that running HTTP-based MCP servers locally without authentication is not recommended per MCP security best practices. This issue does not affect servers using stdio transport. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.24.0.

extended_information.short_description: Lack of DNS rebinding protection in MCP typescript-sdk allows attackers to communicate with local MCP servers that lack authentication, when surfing to untrusted websites
extended_information.full_description:
The [MCP TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) implements the full MCP specification, making it easy to create MCP servers, build MCP clients and use standard transports like stdio and Streamable HTTP
It was discovered that the MCP Typescript SDK did not enforce DNS rebinding protection by default. In a scenario where a MCP server is created using the SDK and -
1. The server is listening on localhost only
2. The server uses HTTP or SSE transport (not STDIO)
3. The server lacks authentication
A user visiting a malicious website on the same machine that runs the server, would allow the website to trigger a DNS rebinding attack via malicious JavaScript code, and send arbitrary data to the locally-running MCP server.

Since some MCP servers expose dangerous tools (such as tools that allow for remote command  execution) exploitation of this issue could lead to remote code execution by malicious websites.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The prerequisites for exploiting the issue are either extremely common or nonexistent (always exploitable)
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description:
It is very likely to use the MCP Typescript SDK in order to create a server with the following properties -
1. The server is listening on localhost only
2. The server uses HTTP or SSE transport (not STDIO)
3. The server lacks authentication

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The issue is trivial to exploit and does not require a published writeup or PoC
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: The attacker simply needs to mount a DNS rebinding attack in order to send arbitrary data to the locally listening MCP server.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: Exploitation of the issue is only possible when the vulnerable component is used in a specific manner. The attacker has to perform per-target research to determine the vulnerable attack vector
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: The attacker would need to know which MCP servers are running on the victim machine, and take advantage of their tools accordingly.

violations.summary: Versions of the package tough-cookie before 4.1.3 are vulnerable to Prototype Pollution due to improper handling of Cookies when using CookieJar in rejectPublicSuffixes=false mode. This issue arises from the manner in which the objects are initialized.

extended_information.short_description: Insufficient input validation in tough-cookie's memstore.js leads to prototype pollution when parsing attacker-controlled cookies.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The prerequisites for exploiting the issue are extremely unlikely
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description:
The library is usually used by a client to retrieve data from a server. 
The attack can occur in one of two scenarios, both highly unlikely:

1. A request is made to a malicious server with the address `__proto__`. Since the character `_` is not a valid DNS character, the malicious server must be located within the same LAN behind a DNS server that supports the invalid character.

2. A man-in-the-middle attack is performed to inject a malicious cookie into a legitimate connection. This is unlikely because the attacker must control the requested URL on the client side.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: Exploitation of the issue is only possible when the vulnerable component is used in a specific manner. The attacker has to perform per-target research to determine the vulnerable attack vector
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description:
An attacker must have control over the cookies being saved in a `cookieJar` object, that is configured with `rejectPublicSuffixes: false` which is not the default value.
When set to `true` (which is the default), this configuration rejects all local URLs without a TLD (for example: `testdomain`, contrary to `testdomain.com`).
Additionally, to execute the attack, one of the following scenarios must occur:
1. A Request is made from the vulnerable client to the malicious server with the address __proto__ which would send a malicious cookie to the client.
2. A Man-in-the-middle attack is performed on an existing connection to inject a malicious cookie to the client.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The issue has an exploit published
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: A public PoC demonstrated exploitation of the vulnerability.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The issue results in a severe impact (such as remote code execution)
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description:
A prototype pollution attack allows the attacker to inject new properties to all JavaScript objects (but not set existing properties).
Therefore, the impact of a prototype pollution attack depends on the way the JavaScript code uses any object properties after the attack is triggered.
Usually, a DoS attack is possible since invalid properties quickly lead to an exception being thrown. In more severe cases, RCE may be achievable.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The reported CVSS was either wrongly calculated, downgraded by other vendors, or does not reflect the vulnerability's impact
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description: CVSS does not take into account the unlikely prerequisites necessary for exploitation.

violations.summary: Useragent is a user agent parser for Node.js. All versions as of time of publication contain one or more regular expressions that are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS). As of time of publication, no patches are available.

BigBlueButton is an open source web conferencing system. Versions starting with 2.2 and prior to 2.3.19, 2.4.7, and 2.5.0-beta.2 are vulnerable to regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) attacks. By using specific a RegularExpression, an attacker can cause denial of service for the bbb-html5 service. The useragent library performs checking of device by parsing the input of User-Agent header and lets it go through lookupUserAgent() (alias of useragent.lookup() ). This function handles input by regexing and attackers can abuse that by providing some ReDos payload using `SmartWatch`. The maintainers removed `htmlclient/useragent` from versions 2.3.19, 2.4.7, and 2.5.0-beta.2. As a workaround, disable NginX forwarding the requests to the handler according to the directions in the GitHub Security Advisory.

A vulnerability was found in Woorank robots-txt-guard. It has been rated as problematic. Affected by this issue is the function makePathPattern of the file lib/patterns.js. The manipulation of the argument pattern leads to inefficient regular expression complexity. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The name of the patch is c03827cd2f9933619c23894ce7c98401ea824020. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-217448.

Anthropic's MCP TypeScript SDK versions up to and including 1.25.1 contain a regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) vulnerability in the UriTemplate class when processing RFC 6570 exploded array patterns. The dynamically generated regular expression used during URI matching contains nested quantifiers that can trigger catastrophic backtracking on specially crafted inputs, resulting in excessive CPU consumption. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a malicious URI that causes the Node.js process to become unresponsive, leading to a denial of service.

violations.summary: MCP TypeScript SDK is the official TypeScript SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. Prior to 1.24.0, The Model Context Protocol (MCP) TypeScript SDK does not enable DNS rebinding protection by default for HTTP-based servers. When an HTTP-based MCP server is run on localhost without authentication with StreamableHTTPServerTransport or SSEServerTransport and has not enabled enableDnsRebindingProtection, a malicious website could exploit DNS rebinding to bypass same-origin policy restrictions and send requests to the local MCP server. This could allow an attacker to invoke tools or access resources exposed by the MCP server on behalf of the user in those limited circumstances. Note that running HTTP-based MCP servers locally without authentication is not recommended per MCP security best practices. This issue does not affect servers using stdio transport. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.24.0.

extended_information.short_description: Lack of DNS rebinding protection in MCP typescript-sdk allows attackers to communicate with local MCP servers that lack authentication, when surfing to untrusted websites
extended_information.full_description:
The [MCP TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) implements the full MCP specification, making it easy to create MCP servers, build MCP clients and use standard transports like stdio and Streamable HTTP
It was discovered that the MCP Typescript SDK did not enforce DNS rebinding protection by default. In a scenario where a MCP server is created using the SDK and -
1. The server is listening on localhost only
2. The server uses HTTP or SSE transport (not STDIO)
3. The server lacks authentication
A user visiting a malicious website on the same machine that runs the server, would allow the website to trigger a DNS rebinding attack via malicious JavaScript code, and send arbitrary data to the locally-running MCP server.

Since some MCP servers expose dangerous tools (such as tools that allow for remote command  execution) exploitation of this issue could lead to remote code execution by malicious websites.

jfrog_research_severity_reasons.name: The prerequisites for exploiting the issue are either extremely common or nonexistent (always exploitable)
jfrog_research_severity_reasons.description:
It is very likely to use the MCP Typescript SDK in order to create a server with the following properties -
1. The server is listening on localhost only
2. The server uses HTTP or SSE transport (not STDIO)
3. The server lacks authentication

violations.summary: SSH clients receiving SSH_AGENT_SUCCESS when expecting a typed response will panic and cause early termination of the client process.

extended_information.short_description: Unhandled data type in crypto/ssh may result in client denial of service when connecting to untrusted SSH agents
extended_information.full_description:
The golang package [x/crypto/ssh](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/crypto/ssh) implements an SSH client and server.
It was found that when a client requests an operation that expects a specific-typed response, the `List()` and the `SignWithFlags()` functions will crash if the response included an unexpected data type, such as the `SSH_AGENT_SUCCESS` (byte `0x06`) message.

An example of a vulnerable client:

```
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent"
)

func main() {
	conn, err := net.Dial("tcp", "127.0.0.1:9999")
	if err != nil { panic(err) }
	ag := agent.NewClient(conn)
	fmt.Println("calling List() — expect panic in agent/client.go")
	_, _ = ag.List() // panics: "unreachable"
}
```
